title: Airbnb Booking System: Complete Architecture
description: Design an Airbnb-scale property booking platform with availability calendars, distributed reservation locks, search, and payments.

data.text: Design a property rental marketplace like Airbnb. Hosts list properties with availability calendars and pricing rules; guests search for properties by location, dates, guest count, and amenities, view detailed listings with photos and reviews, and book with instant or request-to-approve flows. The critical challenge is the distributed reservation problem: preventing double-bookings when multiple guests attempt to book the same property for the same dates simultaneously, while keeping availability search fast.

terms.definition: Assume no conflict; validate at commit time using version numbers. Good for low contention.
Reserve a lock before operation using Redis SETNX or database-level locks. Prevents concurrent writes to the same resource.
Per-property calendar tracking blocked dates (already booked or host-blocked) and pricing rules.
Client-generated UUID sent with booking request to ensure retried requests don't create duplicate bookings.
Search properties within a map viewport using PostGIS or Elasticsearch geo_distance queries.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Hosts list properties with photos, description, amenities, house rules, and calendar pricing
Search properties by: location (map bounds), check-in/check-out dates, guests, filters (price, amenities, property type)
Real-time availability: show only properties available for requested dates
Booking flow: instant book (auto-confirm) or request-to-approve (host accepts/declines in 24h)
Payment: charge guest on booking; payout host 24h after check-in
Cancellation with tiered refund policies (flexible, moderate, strict)
Dual-sided reviews: guest reviews property; host reviews guest after checkout
Messaging between host and guest before/during stay

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: 150 million registered users; 7 million active listings
Booking QPS: ~1,000 concurrent booking attempts during peak (holiday events)
No double-bookings: highest data consistency requirement
Availability search must reflect confirmed bookings within 1 second
Photo storage: 7M listings × ~30 photos × 1MB avg = 210 TB

data.caption: Distributed lock sequence: two concurrent guests attempting to book the same property for overlapping dates — only one succeeds
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant G1 as 👤 Guest 1
    participant G2 as 👤 Guest 2
    participant API as 📋 Booking API
    participant Redis as 🔒 Redis Lock
    participant DB as 🗄️ Booking DB
    participant Cal as 📅 Availability Calendar

    par Concurrent booking requests
        G1->>API: POST /book {prop: A, dates: Jun 1-5, idem_key: uuid1}
        G2->>API: POST /book {prop: A, dates: Jun 1-5, idem_key: uuid2}
    end

    API->>Redis: SETNX lock:propA:Jun1-5 G1 EX 600
    Redis-->>API: OK (G1 gets lock)

    API->>Redis: SETNX lock:propA:Jun1-5 G2 EX 600
    Redis-->>API: FAIL (lock held by G1)
    API-->>G2: 409 Conflict — "Dates being booked, try again"

    Note over API, DB: G1 proceeds with SAGA
    API->>DB: INSERT booking (G1, propA, Jun1-5) idempotency_key=uuid1
    DB-->>API: booking_id=789
    API->>Cal: Mark Jun 1-5 as BOOKED for propA
    Cal-->>API: Updated
    API->>Redis: DEL lock:propA:Jun1-5 (release lock)
    API-->>G1: 201 Created — booking confirmed

    G2->>API: Retry GET /availability {prop: A, Jun 1-5}
    API-->>G2: 410 — Dates no longer available

items.question: Why Redis SETNX for the reservation lock instead of database locking?
items.answer: Database-level SERIALIZABLE isolation works but creates long-held locks that block other transactions and reduce throughput. Redis SETNX (Set if Not eXists) with TTL is a lightweight distributed lock that expires automatically if the booking service crashes, preventing stuck locks. The trade-off is Redis must be highly available (Redis Sentinel / Cluster).

items.question: How do you prevent the booking from going through if payment fails?
items.answer: The booking uses the SAGA pattern: (1) Acquire lock, (2) Create a PENDING booking record, (3) Charge the guest via Stripe, (4) On payment success: mark booking CONFIRMED and update calendar; on payment failure: mark booking CANCELLED and release the lock and calendar. Compensating transactions ensure atomicity across services.

items.question: How does search stay fast with 7M listings and availability filtering?
items.answer: Availability is pre-indexed in Elasticsearch. When a booking is confirmed, a Kafka event triggers an async update to the search index marking those dates as unavailable. Search filters by date range on the index directly — no join to the calendar DB needed. Acceptable eventual consistency: up to 1-2s lag after booking confirmation.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Double-booking prevention requires distributed locking (Redis SETNX) + SERIALIZABLE DB transactions
SAGA pattern with compensating transactions handles cross-service atomicity (lock → charge → confirm)
Availability calendar is the source of truth; search index is an eventually-consistent projection
Idempotency keys prevent duplicate bookings from client retries
Escrow pattern for payments: charge on booking, release to host 24h after check-in
data.takeaway: Airbnb's hardest problem is the distributed reservation: guaranteeing no two guests can book the same property for the same dates, while keeping search fast enough to serve 50K queries per second.
